ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 3
SUBJECT: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water its resources? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water its resources.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water its resources.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water its resources.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water its resources.

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Keeping safe from? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Keeping safe from.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Keeping safe from.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Keeping safe from.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Keeping safe from.

4. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Keeping safe in? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Keeping safe in.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Keeping safe in.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Keeping safe in.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Keeping safe in.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Plants and its resources? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Plants and its resources.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Plants and its resources.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Plants and its resources.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Plants and its resources.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animals and its resources? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Animals and its resources.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animals and its resources.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animals and its resources.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animals and its resources.

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

11. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy: Heat and its resources? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy: Heat and its resources.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Energy: Heat and its resources.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy: Heat and its resources.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy: Heat and its resources.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Animals and its resources and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Energy: Heat and its resources and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Uses of heat in and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Dangers of heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water its resources.

2. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Keeping safe from.

4. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

5. C — Ice melting to water

6. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Keeping safe in.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Plants and its resources.

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animals and its resources.

10. B — Producers

11. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy: Heat and its resources.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animals and its resources; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Uses of heat in; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Dangers of heat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
